title: Generic object = whole Word; special object = Gospel promises — as saving, not as exclusive
source_text: XC. Quod spectat fidei salvificae objectum, observatum est Doctores Reformatos plerosque distinguere inter objectum fidei adaequatum, genericum & commune, & inter ejus objectum proprium, & speciale, sive specificum. Objectum genericum & commune dicunt esse totum Dei Verbum, seu quicquid est credenti a Deo revelatum. Proprium vero, specificum, & speciale, promissiones Evangelii. Quod ut recte intelligatur, notandum est, dum Reformati dicunt objectum speciale & proprium fidei salvificae & justificantis, esse promissiones Evangelii, mentem eorum non esse, quod objectum istud ita sit justificantis fidei proprium, ut non sit etiam objectum fidei historicae. Fides enim historica, ex eorum hypothesi, credit veras esse Dei promissiones, non minus quam historias, quae in Verbo Dei narrantur. Sed promissiones Evangelicas docent esse proprium objectum fidei justificantis, quia fides quatenus salvat & justificat, circa promissiones illas proprie versatur. Et hoc est quod alii dicunt, totum Dei Verbum esse objectum fidei quae justificat, sed promissiones Evangelii esse objectum ejus qua justificat.
pass_a_gloss: As to the object of saving faith, it has been observed that most Reformed Doctors distinguish between the adequate, generic, and common object of faith, and its proper and special, or specific, object. They say the generic and common object is the whole Word of God, or whatever has been revealed by God to the believer. But the proper, specific, and special is the promises of the Gospel. Which, that it may be rightly understood, it is to be noted that when the Reformed say the special and proper object of saving and justifying faith is the promises of the Gospel, their mind is not that that object is so proper to justifying faith that it is not also an object of historical faith. For historical faith, on their hypothesis, believes God's promises to be true no less than the histories which are narrated in the Word of God. But they teach that the Gospel promises are the proper object of justifying faith, because faith inasmuch as it saves and justifies is properly conversant about those promises. And this is what others say: the whole Word of God is the object of the faith which justifies, but the promises of the Gospel are the object of it whereby it justifies.
pass_b_english: Most Reformed: adequate/generic object of faith = the whole Word; proper/special = Gospel promises.
Not that promises belong only to justifying faith — historical faith also believes them true, as it believes the histories.
Promises are “proper” because faith as saving and justifying is specially conversant about them.
So: whole Word is object of the faith that justifies; Gospel promises are the object whereby it justifies.
